rubrics.justification: The response appropriately identifies a good-quality expanded blastocyst with thinning zona and notes possible partial collapse/asymmetry. ICM and TE descriptions are generally consistent with the reported 3AA, though some image-based claims about dense ICM and cohesive TE are somewhat limited by the single focal plane and image quality.

It integrates age, BMI, FSH, tubal factor, prior IVF history, semen parameters, endometrial thickness, and smoking status well, and explains how these factors modify prognosis alongside embryo quality.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with conclusions generally supported by morphology and clinical context. Minor issues include somewhat overstated certainty from a single image and an arguably strong claim about smoking reducing implantation by 10–20% absolute.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice and Gardner grading principles, including attention to hydrosalpinx, luteal support, and cautious use of PGT-A. Small deviations include overprecision in aneuploidy estimates and some non-guideline lifestyle advice phrasing.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including smoking cessation, hydrosalpinx review, luteal support, and uterine cavity assessment. Useful overall, though some recommendations remain somewhat general rather than protocol-specific.
